articles.title: SJAA Potluck and Awards Ceremony
articles.summary: The San Jose Astronomical Association (SJAA) recently hosted its first post-pandemic potluck and awards ceremony on February 24, 2024, gathering over 20 attendees. During the event, Rob Jaworski and Swami Nigam received the prestigious Doctor A.B. Gregory Award for their significant contributions to amateur astronomy and the club. Additionally, several other members, including Renuka Veeraswami, Jonathan Lawton, and Joe Fragola, were honored with Volunteer Awards for their diverse efforts in outreach, education, and club operations.

articles.title: Introducing Director 9
articles.summary: Marianne Damon has been appointed to the Director 9 position on the Board of Directors, filling the vacancy left by Sukhada Palav. A long-time member since 2013, Damon is known for her extensive involvement in SJAA outreach events, creating astronomy-themed activities, and contributing to internal club initiatives like the 24" Dob Task Force and Compliance Team. She shares her lifelong passion for astronomy, which she has actively pursued since retiring, and mentions her upcoming trip for the Total Solar Eclipse.

articles.title: Introducing Speaker and Fix It Program Leaders
articles.summary: The SJAA announces two new program leaders: Larry Zurbick for the returning 'Fix It' program, which offers assistance with telescope collimation, mechanical adjustments, and minor repairs on the first Sunday of each month, and Leo Lipkin as the new Speaker Coordinator. Zurbick brings decades of amateur astronomy experience, while Lipkin, a Firmware Test Engineer, will connect members with engaging speakers. Both roles aim to enhance member services and club activities.

articles.title: Radio Signals From Space
articles.summary: An amateur radio operator and astronomer, tuning 10- and 15-meter bands during high sunspot activity, encountered unusual radio signals leading to research into natural radio emissions from celestial bodies like the Sun, Earth, and Jupiter. The article explains how electrons accelerated through magnetic fields emit radio waves, noting that Jupiter's emissions (enhanced by Io) are theoretically detectable by amateur equipment. It then provides practical methods for enthusiasts to detect and observe these signals, including using Radio JOVE kits, online spectrographs, and NASA's project website, alongside tools for tracking Jupiter's position.

articles.title: SJAA Member Astrophoto Gallery
articles.summary: This article presents a gallery of astrophotography images captured by members of the SJAA (San Jose Astronomical Association). Each entry features a specific celestial object, such as the IC 342 Galaxy or the Tadpoles Nebula, and provides detailed information including the photographer's name, capture dates, location, and the specific telescope, camera, mount, and software used for imaging and processing.

articles.title: Fight the Dew
articles.summary: This article addresses the common problem of dew in amateur astronomy, explaining how water droplets form on telescope lenses and mirrors, often ruining observing sessions. It details two primary prevention methods: active dew heaters and passive dew shields, noting their respective advantages and disadvantages. The author also provides practical DIY solutions, including a simple cardboard shield and a more advanced 3D-printed design, encouraging astronomers to combat dew creatively and affordably.

articles.title: The comet C/2023 A3 (Tsuchinан-ATLAS) could be the next Hale-Bopp
articles.summary: Comet C/2023 A3 (Tsuchinshan-ATLAS), originating from the Oort cloud, is predicted to become visible to the naked eye in October 2024, passing closest to Earth on October 12, 2024. Currently, the comet is in Libra with a magnitude of 13, requiring long-exposure astroimaging for observation, as demonstrated by recent images taken from Australia. Its light curve suggests it could be a significant astronomical event, potentially comparable to Hale-Bopp.

articles.title: OBSERVING HIGHLIGHTS
articles.summary: This article highlights key astronomical events from March to June, including equinoxes, solstices, lunar and solar eclipses, and prominent meteor showers. It provides specific dates and brief descriptions for each event, such as the Spring Equinox, Penumbral Lunar Eclipse, Total Solar Eclipse, and the Lyrid and Eta Aquarid meteor showers. Additionally, it lists dates for Mercury's greatest elongations and the phases of the New Moon and Full Moon during this period.

articles.title: From the Board of Directors
articles.summary: The Board of Directors announced the re-election of Rob Jaworski, Glenn Newell, and Wolf Witt, along with the election of Radhika Gupta, to the board until February 2026. Upcoming officer elections for President, Vice-President, Treasurer, and Secretary will be held online, and new appointments include Leo Lipkin as Speaker Coordinator. Board meetings on January 27 and February 24, 2024, approved expenditures for a website plugin, new fence banners, and A/V equipment for Houge Park, and discussed open positions for Librarian and Astronomy 101 leader.

articles.title: SJAA Library
articles.summary: The San Jose Astronomical Association (SJAA) provides a diverse range of resources and programs for its members and the wider community. Offerings include a library, a free Telescope Fix It service, and a Loaner Program for astronomy equipment. SJAA also hosts various observing sessions, educational programs like Quick STARt and Intro to the Night Sky, specialized astrophotography groups and workshops, and conducts outreach through School Star Parties.
